messages.subject: Re: Standard Error or Standard Deviation
parts:
Hi Koustubh, list,

If you are comparing two density estimates, your single-factor ANOVA is the same
as the t-test described in Section 3.6.5 of Introduction to Distance Sampling. It
describes there how to obtain the standard error of the difference in densities.
When the two estimates are independent, simply add the variances. Where they
share some component of estimation (such as f(0)) things are a little more complex
as outlined in the section (although it isn't a good idea to estimate a pooled f
(0) unless you have to, because changes in abundance may then be confounded with
changes in detectability).

The same approach can be taken using ANOVA and you will get the same result. You
want to use the standard errors of the estimates in calculating the error mean
square.

> >If this is true, I have a little problem in case of calculation of CV, which is
> >CV = s / Mean ...(2)

On page 424 of the book (the Glossary) we define CV as standard error/estimate.
Either definition is "correct", but it's important to be clear about which one is
being used in a particular context.

Hope this helps,

- Len
